touches.text: QUESTIONS: a question is [Q#n: ...], placed at the line it bears on. Its #n is its own and never changes; a new one takes the next unused number, which is now 124. An answered question disappears: its answer is folded into the intention and why (0.2.1), and signed where it records a decision (0.5). Why? Becuase too many words makes it hard for both akien and Claude to understand.

Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing.
corrosion: catches a constraint that stopped constraining with no decision behind it. WHY: drift with a decision behind it is the system learning; drift with none is decay.

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).

conflicts.text: Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing.
conflicts.ticket_says: withdrawn questions stop holding the build (resolved=True, answer=None) even when not answered by an operator
conflicts.why: The outline states: 'An open question in those sections... becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered.' The ticket allows questions to stop holding the build without being answered—contradicting the 'until answered' condition. The outline treats 'answered' as the sole mechanism to clear the hold; the ticket adds withdrawal as an alternative path that bypasses this requirement.
